text: Direct judgment inventory in .skilled (excluding tests/benchmarks): 7 choice call sites (verdict-fallback:783, severity-replay:1070, jev-tiebreak:1005, suggested-order, debug-next-check:733, track-narrowing:1327, alignment-suggestion.ts:1083); 7+ noul (cite-drift-scan:1081, goal-lint:313, severity-replay:1118, fanout-pairs:985, residue-flagger:1093, completion-claims:784, jev-tiebreak:928); 1 score (stop-rater:1090).
The two wired callers are both offline measurement harnesses in sk-doc; no production caller has adopted the transport, so live-workflow payoff is still zero.

Largest call-volume surface is the routing-accuracy pair: 333 choice calls per 111-row replay. Pi re-route saves about 25 s wall time and $0.0075 per replay at the catalog price; the harness is operator-run, not on a live path.

Deep-loop runtime scorers are closest to workflow critical paths but blocked by type: severity-replay (choice+noul), fanout-pairs (noul), residue-flagger (noul), stop-rater (score) each need their own keep-rule run; the transport decides only for choice by REQ-003.

The transport's payoff is operational, not epistemic: same model family both routes, 95.5 agreement; gains are ~22 pct mean latency, one fewer child process, and a route that needs no jev binary when a Pi credential exists.

A Pi-native call is invisible to dispatch auditing: dispatch-audit classifies jev choice|noul|score|run (and jev-mcp) as cli-classifier dispatches; adopting the transport inside dispatch-tracked scripts narrows what the audit sees.

cli-pi documents the three native classifier surfaces for Pi workers (codemode models.classify up to 4 concurrent, extensions, SDK), but the only code in .skilled calling native classify today is the benchmark and the transport itself.
Two surfaces are out of scope on inspection: score-stop-hint replays a rater report offline (reads the jev column, no classifier spawn); dispatch-audit only classifies a jev invocation.

Adoption payoff ranking: routing-accuracy harnesses own volume but run occasionally; debug-next-check and goal-lint are interactive with small counts; deep-loop scorers gain critical-path latency but need bool/score measurement; no surface gains accuracy anywhere.
sk-doc noul callers (cite-drift-scan, goal-lint) are outside the 13-caller list yet reachable by the same seam; if a bool arm is ever measured they are the cheapest early adopters.
